\section[tribūnal, tribūnālis]{tribūnal, tribūnālis — the judgement seat, a raised platform}

\label{lesson:LA-C411-tribunal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for to make sacred and binding, then the Latin for to lay down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: tribūnal, tribūnālis}
\textbf{tribūnal, tribūnālis} — \textquotedblleft{}the judgement seat, a raised platform\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Praetor in tribūnālī sedēbat.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The praetor sat on the judgement seat.}
\end{quote}

\emph{tribūnal, tribūnālis} n.: the raised platform where a magistrate sat to judge. English \emph{tribunal}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tribūnal} is built on \emph{tribūnus} \textquotedblleft{}a tribune\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), who takes his name from \emph{tribus} \textquotedblleft{}a tribe\textquotedblright{}: the platform of the tribunes. English \emph{tribunal} comes from it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tribūnal, tribūnālis}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tribūnal, tribūnālis}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tribūnal, tribūnālis}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for to make sacred and binding, then the Latin for to lay down, then say \emph{tribūnal, tribūnālis} again
\end{itemize}

\section[līs, lītis]{līs, lītis — a lawsuit, a dispute}

\label{lesson:LA-C411-lis}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for to lay down, then the Latin for the judgement seat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: līs, lītis}
\textbf{līs, lītis} — \textquotedblleft{}a lawsuit, a dispute\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Inter frātrēs līs dē hērēditāte erat.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There was a lawsuit between the brothers about the inheritance.}
\end{quote}

\emph{līs, lītis} f., old Latin \emph{stlīs}. \emph{Lītem intendere}, to bring a suit. English \emph{litigation} is built on it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{līs} was \emph{stlīs} in old Latin (EtymDB; Lewis \& Short); its deeper origin is not settled. English \emph{litigation} comes from its family.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{līs, lītis}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{līs, lītis}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{līs, lītis}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for to lay down, then the Latin for the judgement seat, then say \emph{līs, lītis} again
\end{itemize}

\section[lītigō, lītigāre]{lītigō, lītigāre — to go to law, to quarrel}

\label{lesson:LA-C411-litigo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for the judgement seat, then the Latin for a lawsuit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: lītigō, lītigāre}
\textbf{lītigō, lītigāre} — \textquotedblleft{}to go to law, to quarrel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Vīcīnī dē fīnibus lītigant.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The neighbours are going to law about the boundaries.}
\end{quote}

\emph{lītigō, lītigāre, lītigāvī, lītigātum}, built on \emph{līs} and \emph{agō}: to drive a suit. English \emph{litigate}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lītigō} is built from \emph{līs, lītis} \textquotedblleft{}a lawsuit\textquotedblright{} and \emph{agō} \textquotedblleft{}to drive, to conduct\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short). English \emph{litigate} comes from it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[vadimōnium, vadimōniī]{vadimōnium, vadimōniī — a promise to appear in court, bail}

\label{lesson:LA-C411-vadimonium}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for a lawsuit, then the Latin for to go to law.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: vadimōnium, vadimōniī}
\textbf{vadimōnium, vadimōniī} — \textquotedblleft{}a promise to appear in court, bail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Reus vadimōnium prōmīsit.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The accused gave bail to appear.}
\end{quote}

\emph{vadimōnium, vadimōniī} n., built on \emph{vas, vadis}, a surety: a promise, backed by money, to appear in court on a set day.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vadimōnium} is built on \emph{vas, vadis} \textquotedblleft{}a surety, a bail\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB; Lewis \& Short), with the ending \emph{-mōnium}; it is a different word from \emph{vās} \textquotedblleft{}a vessel\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vadimōnium, vadimōniī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{vadimōnium, vadimōniī}

\section[iūriscōnsultus, iūriscōnsultī]{iūriscōnsultus, iūriscōnsultī — a legal expert, a jurist}

\label{lesson:LA-C411-iurisconsultus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for to go to law, then the Latin for a promise to appear in court.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: iūriscōnsultus, iūriscōnsultī}
\textbf{iūriscōnsultus, iūriscōnsultī} — \textquotedblleft{}a legal expert, a jurist\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Iūriscōnsultum dē hāc rē cōnsuluī.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I consulted a legal expert about this matter.}
\end{quote}

\emph{iūriscōnsultus, iūriscōnsultī} m., also written as two words, \emph{iūris cōnsultus}: one consulted on the law. Romans came to his house in the morning for advice.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{iūriscōnsultus} is built from \emph{iūris} \textquotedblleft{}of the law\textquotedblright{}, the genitive of \emph{iūs}, and \emph{cōnsultus}, the participle of \emph{cōnsulō} \textquotedblleft{}to consult\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB; Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{iūriscōnsultus, iūriscōnsultī}
